                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable github.com/dhax/go-base package present in software inventory — CVE-2026-48031 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Hardcoded AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random pattern in dev.env / source artifacts
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] go-base admin/auth endpoint access — CVE-2026-48031 exploitation indicator
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JWT bearer token with extreme far-future expiration to go-base endpoints
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
go-base admin/auth endpoint access — CVE-2026-48031 exploitation indicator AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP traffic to the dhax/go-base CVE-2026-48031 high-value endpoints (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh) bearing an Authorization: Bearer JWT header from a source that has never previously authenticated to the host. The article confirms forged HS256 tokens signed with the literal string 'random' will be accepted on every protected endpoint, so successful (HTTP 200) requests to admin-tier URIs from a new client IP are the cleanest exploitation telemetry available pre-patch. Rationale: All five matching URIs are the literal endpoints from the article's PoC (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh). Successful (HTTP 200) responses confirm the forged token was accepted by the vulnerable jwtauth.New('HS256', ...) verifier. W3CIISLog uses Computer (its host column) instead of DeviceName.
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1606.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin user genuinely calling /api/v1/admin/users after authenticating via the password-less flow
  • Internal QA / smoke tests hitting /api/v1/me with valid tokens
  • Monitoring / synthetic probes against /api/v1/token/refresh with a service-account token
  • First successful login post-patch where the secret has been rotated but the same URI is hit
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","safari.exe") and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Decode the Authorization bearer JWT on the request and check the kid/alg/iss/exp claims; attempt verification with HMAC-SHA256 secret 'random' — if the signature validates, treat as confirmed forgery. Pull the client IP's prior 30-day history against this host. Step 2 (contain): Block the offending source IP at the WAF/CDN, force-rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET on the affected go-base instance (openssl rand -base64 32), redeploy, invalidate all outstanding refresh tokens, and require re-authentication. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the client IP across /api/v1/* to see what data was enumerated; review user-table reads, account modifications, and any token-refresh calls that issued new long-lived tokens; check git history for any other repos using 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random'.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (3000, 8080, 80, 443)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has_any (GoBasePaths)
  | where scStatus == 200
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iif(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName, Source="W3CIISLog"
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (GoBasePaths)
  | where DeviceAction !~ "deny"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Url=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Status=EventOutcome, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName, Source="CommonSecurityLog"
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any (GoBasePaths)
  | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Url, Method=HttpMethod, Status=HttpStatusCode, UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, User=SrcUsername, Source="ImWebSession"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hardcoded AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random pattern in dev.env / source artifacts AIWeaponization High
Hunts file writes or reads of dev.env (or any .env-family file) that contain the literal string 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' — the exact template default shipped by github.com/dhax/go-base. Catches both ongoing developer copies of the vulnerable template into prod-bound repos/containers and historical artifacts on disk. Rationale: dev.env is named literally at article line 10 as the artifact carrying AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random. Catching its appearance on prod hosts or in CI artifacts flags every copy of the vulnerable boilerplate before exploitation. Content inspection (the AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random string) is best layered via secret-scanning, but file-name + go-base path is high-fidelity by itself.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers cloning go-base intentionally into a sandboxed lab
  • Legitimate CI step extracting an .env template before substitution
  • Backup / restore operations replaying a previously-cleaned dev.env
  • DevContainer / Codespaces provisioning that drops .env from a template
Suppression filter
| where TargetFilePath !has_any ("\\test\\","\\fixtures\\","\\sandbox\\","\\lab\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the file contents on disk (or in the artifact) for the literal string 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' and confirm whether the host is running the dhax/go-base binary on an exposed port. Step 2 (contain): If the host serves traffic, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32-byte random value (openssl rand -base64 32), redeploy, and invalidate outstanding refresh tokens; remove dev.env from version control history (git filter-repo) and from container layers. Step 3 (hunt): Search source-code repositories, container registries, and S3 / blob artifact stores for the same string; correlate with UC1 to see if any forged-token traffic has already hit /api/v1/admin endpoints.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("dev.env",".env",".env.example",".env.dev",".env.local","app.env")
   or FolderPath has_any ("\\go-base\\","/go-base/","dhax")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("dev.env",".env",".env.example",".env.dev",".env.local","app.env")
   or TargetFilePath has_any ("\\go-base\\","/go-base/","dhax")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable github.com/dhax/go-base package present in software inventory — CVE-2026-48031 AIReconnaissance High
Asset-exposure hunt that matches DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory / DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities against the vulnerable go-base versions (anything prior to commit 0.0.0-20260517152733-cc82b9740fa6). Surfaces every host running the JWT-forge-vulnerable boilerplate so it can be patched before exploitation. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the natural Defender/Sentinel pivot for CVE-based asset exposure. Matching on both CveId and SoftwareVendor=dhax + SoftwareName has 'go-base' catches inventories where CVE enrichment lags. Internet-facing flag elevates priority.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandboxed lab / training hosts running vulnerable go-base intentionally
  • Decommissioned hosts still in inventory but no longer serving
  • SBOM scanner that tags the vendored module without confirming the running binary
  • Forked copies of go-base where the JWT secret has already been replaced manually
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each matched host, confirm the go-base binary is actually serving traffic (check listening port 3000/8080) and whether AUTH_JWT_SECRET is still 'random' via a controlled probe. Step 2 (contain): Prioritise patching internet-facing hosts (IsInternetFacing == true); apply PR#31 (post-2026-05-17 master) or rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET out-of-band and add a startup gate refusing 'random'/'secret'/'changeme'/empty. Step 3 (hunt): Roll UC1 (admin-endpoint access) against the same DeviceId list back-in-time 30 days to scope possible prior exploitation; check for any new privileged AAD/IAM accounts created during the window.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48031"
   or (SoftwareVendor =~ "dhax" and SoftwareName has "go-base")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup, OSPlatform
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48031"
   or (SoftwareVendor =~ "dhax" and SoftwareName has "go-base")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup, OSPlatform
  ) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc

JWT bearer token with extreme far-future expiration to go-base endpoints AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts Authorization: Bearer JWTs sent to dhax/go-base endpoints whose decoded exp claim is more than 1 year beyond the request time — the article's PoC sets exp=9999999999 (year 2286), a near-pathognomonic forge signature. Pairs the URI from UC1 with a content-of-JWT predicate captured by the reverse proxy / API gateway. Rationale: The PoC at the article sets exp=9999999999 and iat=9999999000 — any production go-base token issued with the patched code uses minute-to-hour lifetimes, so exp > now+365d on a successful /api/v1/* request is a high-fidelity forge indicator. Sentinel KQL decodes the JWT payload inline; Defender DeviceNetworkEvents lacks header inspection so the runbook routes analysts to the proxy log.
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate long-lived service-account tokens issued for machine-to-machine integrations (rare in go-base but possible)
  • CI / synthetic monitoring tokens deliberately minted with year+ exp
  • Test tokens left in staging by developers
  • Misconfigured token lifetime policy on the application itself (legit but worth flagging)
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and Sub !has_any ("healthcheck","synthetic-probe","ci-runner")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Verify the bearer token signature against HS256 secret 'random' — if it validates, the token is forged. Compare the decoded sub/roles claim against IdentityInfo for the same user. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET on the affected host, invalidate all refresh tokens, and force re-authentication for every active session. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the source IP across all /api/v1/* URIs over the last 30 days; review admin-tier responses for data egress; check if any new IAM/AAD principals were created during the window; verify the host has been patched per PR#31.
// Defender does not decode JWT payloads; emit the URI hit and let the analyst inspect the captured Authorization header at the proxy.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","safari.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any (GoBasePaths)
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| extend BearerToken = extract(@"(?i)Bearer\s+([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", 1, tostring(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization))
| where isnotempty(BearerToken)
| extend PayloadB64 = extract(@"^[^.]+\.([^.]+)\.", 1, BearerToken)
| extend PayloadB64Padded = strcat(PayloadB64, substring("====", 0, (4 - strlen(PayloadB64) % 4) % 4))
| extend PayloadB64Std = replace_string(replace_string(PayloadB64Padded, "-", "+"), "_", "/")
| extend PayloadJson = base64_decode_tostring(PayloadB64Std)
| extend Claims = parse_json(PayloadJson)
| extend ExpSeconds = tolong(Claims.exp), Sub = tostring(Claims.sub), Roles = tostring(Claims.roles)
| extend ExpDateTime = unixtime_seconds_todatetime(ExpSeconds)
| where ExpDateTime > now() + 365d
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, Sub, Roles, ExpDateTime, BearerToken
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:traefik OR source:envoy) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/admin* OR */api/v1/me* OR */api/v1/token/refresh*) @http.request.headers.authorization:Bearer*

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)Authorization:\s*Bearer\s+(?<jwt>[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)" | where isnotnull(jwt) | rex field=jwt "^[^.]+\.(?<payload_b64>[^.]+)\." | eval payload_b64=replace(payload_b64,"-","+") | eval payload_b64=replace(payload_b64,"_","/") | eval payload=urldecode(base64decode(payload_b64)) | rex field=payload "\"exp\":\s*(?<exp>\d+)" | eval exp_seconds=tonumber(exp), now_s=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%s")), exp_minus_now=exp_seconds-now_s | where exp_minus_now > 31536000 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)Authorization:\s*Bearer\s+(?<jwt>[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)" | where isnotnull(jwt) | rex field=jwt "^[^.]+\.(?<payload_b64>[^.]+)\." | eval payload_b64=replace(payload_b64,"-","+") | eval payload_b64=replace(payload_b64,"_","/") | eval payload=urldecode(base64decode(payload_b64)) | rex field=payload "\"exp\":\s*(?<exp>\d+)" | eval exp_seconds=tonumber(exp), now_s=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%s")), exp_minus_now=exp_seconds-now_s | where exp_minus_now > 31536000 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 9 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Cargo build-script-build process for compromised onering crate · [LLM] Cargo build script spawning network or shell utilities · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Network callback to onering supply-chain Sentry ingest endpoint · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Build-time git log/diff invocation matching onering exfiltration pattern · [LLM] curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint from Cargo build context · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Network callback to onering supply-chain Sentry ingest endpoint AICommand & Control High
Detects any host resolving or connecting to the Sentry ingest hostname / DSN project hard-coded in the malicious onering 1.4.1 build.rs. The endpoint is unique to the attacker's Sentry tenant and is the exfiltration channel for git commit diffs. Rationale: The Sentry organization id o4511539639222272 / project id 4511539669368912 and the FQDN o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io are unique strings that the article and a corroborating Hacker News write-up both attribute solely to this campaign. Cross-checked: Aikido blog (primary) and cyberwebspider/Hacker News summary of the onering compromise — same DSN keys. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://cyberwebspider.com/the-hacker-news/malicious-rust-crates-ai-bot-threat/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A different team in the org legitimately uses Sentry — but those will have a different organization id / project id, so this exact host should never match
  • Internal security tooling re-fetching the article and following the URL during research
  • DNS resolver caching tests that probe known-bad IOCs (DNS sinkhole feed validation)
  • Researcher / IR analyst manually curling the IOC to verify takedown status
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot from the matching device to all build hosts and laptops that compiled it; pull the parent process tree of the network call — confirm the initiator is build-script-build (or build_script_build on Linux) under cargo. Pull `git log` / `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` evidence from the same window. 2) Contain: isolate the device(s); revoke any source-code repo tokens cached on those hosts; rotate any secrets that may have been in the leaked diffs; remove onering 1.4.1 from Cargo.lock and yank/pin to a safe earlier version; flush DNS and add network block on the Sentry tenant id. 3) Hunt: search the last 90 days for the same domain across all telemetry; enumerate every repo that imported onering directly or transitively (`cargo tree | grep onering`) and treat each commit pushed since the first hit as potentially leaked.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
    or RemoteUrl has "4511539669368912/envelope"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery =~ "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, EventProduct),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io" or Url has "4511539669368912/envelope"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, EventProduct),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io" or DestinationHostName =~ "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DeviceProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo build-script-build process for compromised onering crate AIInstallation High
Detects execution of the onering crate's compiled build.rs (Cargo names the artifact build-script-build inside target/<profile>/build/onering-<hash>/). This is the actual malicious payload — running it triggers the git theft and Sentry POST, so seeing it execute on any host is high-fidelity even if the network call later fails. Rationale: `target/<profile>/build/<crate>-<hash>/build-script-build` is the deterministic path Cargo emits when it compiles a crate's build.rs — pivoting on `onering-` inside that path catches the malicious payload regardless of crate version or registry source (so it also catches the git-pulled compromised copy the article warns about). Cross-checked with Cargo Book build-script artifact layout. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A security researcher intentionally detonating the crate in a sandbox
  • An organization that legitimately pins onering for testing the fix once a clean version is published
  • Forensic replay of a pulled FDR/Defender dataset on an analyst workstation
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SHA256 of the build-script-build artifact and the cargo.exe / rustc.exe parent chain; check whether the same host generated a network event to o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io within 60s. 2) Contain: kill the cargo process group, wipe target/debug/build/onering-* and target/release/build/onering-* on the host, remove onering 1.4.1 from Cargo.lock, and require a clean rebuild from a pinned safe version. 3) Hunt: search across all developer and CI hosts for the same FolderPath pattern; cross-correlate with `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` invocations (UC: build-time git exfiltration commands) to confirm whether the payload completed end-to-end.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\target\debug\build\onering-" or FolderPath has @"\target\release\build\onering-"
      or FolderPath has "/target/debug/build/onering-" or FolderPath has "/target/release/build/onering-")
| where FileName has "build-script-build" or FileName has "build_script_build"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetProcessName has @"\target\debug\build\onering-" or TargetProcessName has @"\target\release\build\onering-"
     or TargetProcessName has "/target/debug/build/onering-" or TargetProcessName has "/target/release/build/onering-")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Build-time git log/diff invocation matching onering exfiltration pattern AIActions on Objectives High
Detects git.exe / git invoked with the precise --pretty=format JSON template or `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` pattern the malicious onering build.rs uses to collect commit metadata and the latest commit's patch, when initiated from a Cargo build context. Catches the collection step even if the C2 POST is sinkholed. Rationale: The article quotes the exact `--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H","author":"%an"...` template and the literal `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` string emitted by the malicious build.rs. Anchoring on those strings AND the Cargo build parent chain (build-script-build / cargo / rustc) eliminates the noise from developers running git interactively while preserving the high-signal supply-chain pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A bespoke build.rs in a local crate that emits commit metadata for embedding a build banner (will typically use a different --pretty template, not both forms)
  • CI pipelines that wrap cargo with a custom commit-stamping script — easily allowlisted by repo path
  • An engineer running `cargo build` immediately after `git log` in the same terminal (parent will be the shell, not build-script-build)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\.cargo\registry\src\" or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the ProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if parent is build-script-build under target/.../onering-*, treat as confirmed onering compromise. Capture which repo path the git commands ran against (working dir). 2) Contain: kill cargo and any spawned curl, isolate the device, rotate any secrets present in recent commits on the affected repo, and revoke the dev's source-code tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same parent path across all build hosts and CI runners; check for follow-on curl POSTs to the Sentry endpoint within 60 seconds; review `git reflog` on affected repos to enumerate which commits were leaked.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe", "git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has @"--pretty=format:{""commit"":""%H"""
    or ProcessCommandLine has "diff HEAD^ HEAD"
    or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)diff\s+HEAD\^\s+HEAD\b"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo.exe", "cargo", "rustc.exe", "rustc")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo.exe", "cargo")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("git.exe", "\\git", "/git")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has @"--pretty=format:{""commit"":""%H"""
     or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)diff\s+HEAD\^\s+HEAD\b"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo", "rustc")
    or ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo", "rustc")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint from Cargo build context AIActions on Objectives High
Detects curl invoked with the Sentry envelope URL or `application/x-sentry-envelope` content-type — the exact exfiltration pattern in the onering build.rs. Tightens to Cargo/build-script parents to suppress legitimate Sentry SDK or DevOps traffic that uses its own client libraries rather than curl. Rationale: Anchors on three strings the article quotes verbatim from the build.rs source: the FQDN, the campaign-unique envelope path `/api/4511539669368912/envelope/`, and the `application/x-sentry-envelope` Content-Type header. All three are unique to this attacker's Sentry tenant; any single one is enough. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://cyberwebspider.com/the-hacker-news/malicious-rust-crates-ai-bot-threat/
ATT&CKT1041 T1567.002 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tooling that uses curl to scan for known-bad IOCs (sinkhole reachability checks)
  • Threat-intel analyst manually validating the IOC during triage
  • Internal write-ups / blog posts copy-pasting the article body that happens to be downloaded with curl
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the curl parent is build-script-build, cargo, rustc, or sh-under-cargo; capture process tree + working directory + the full POST cmdline; treat any developer machine match as a true positive. 2) Contain: isolate device; revoke source-code repo tokens accessed in the last 30 days; remove onering 1.4.1 from Cargo.lock and rebuild from a known-good pin; rotate any secrets that appear in recent commit diffs. 3) Hunt: pivot on parent_process_name=build-script-build* across the fleet for a 90-day window; cross-correlate with the C2-domain UC; review CI logs for any pipeline that built a crate transitively depending on onering.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe", "curl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
        "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io",
        "application/x-sentry-envelope",
        "/api/4511539669368912/envelope"
      )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("\\curl.exe", "/curl")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (
        "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io",
        "application/x-sentry-envelope",
        "/api/4511539669368912/envelope"
      )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo build script spawning network or shell utilities AIInstallation Medium
Hunting query that surfaces any Cargo build-script-build process spawning network egress / shell / archival tools (curl, wget, powershell, bitsadmin, certutil, sh, bash, tar, zip). The malicious onering build.rs is one instance of a wider pattern — build.rs spawning anything network-shaped is unusual and worth a triage queue. Rationale: build.rs is supposed to compile/inspect code, not call out to curl/git/shells. The article shows onering's build.rs spawning exactly that pattern (curl POST + git log + git diff). Extracting the crate name from the build path lets analysts group the noise per-crate, so a single noisy custom build.rs in-house doesn't drown the rare external-crate hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/five-malicious-rust-crates-and-ai-bot.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crates that legitimately invoke `git` from build.rs to embed a commit hash (e.g. via the `vergen` or `built` crates) — common and benign
  • Crates that download native dependencies in build.rs (e.g. `openssl-sys` calling curl/git for vendored sources, `cmake`-driven C deps)
  • Internal CI scripts that wrap `cargo build` in a shell that itself spawns curl as a sibling — parent chain will not include build-script-build
  • Diesel / sqlx build scripts running `cargo` again recursively
Suppression filter
| where CrateBuildScript !in~ ("vergen", "built", "openssl-sys", "cmake", "cc", "bindgen", "protobuf-codegen")
Response runbook
1) Triage: group hits by `CrateBuildScript` value — known-benign crates (vergen, built, openssl-sys, cmake) become an allowlist; unfamiliar crate names get prioritized. For unknown crates, pull the crate name + version from Cargo.lock on the host. 2) Contain: if the crate is unknown or recently-added, treat as suspected supply-chain compromise — kill cargo, isolate device, and pull build artifacts for malware analysis. 3) Hunt: pivot on the suspect crate name into all dependency manifests (`Cargo.lock`) across the org to enumerate blast radius; cross-correlate to the network-egress UCs above to confirm exfiltration intent.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/][^\\/]+[\\/]"
| where FileName in~ (
        "curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget",
        "powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
        "git.exe","git","tar.exe","tar","zip.exe","zip","7z.exe",
        "sh","bash","cmd.exe","nc.exe","nc","ncat.exe","ncat"
      )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Hits = count(), SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
               CrateBuildScript = tostring(extract(@"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](?:debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/]([^\\/]+)[\\/]", 1, InitiatingProcessFolderPath))
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build")
   or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/][^\\/]+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build"
| where TargetProcessName has_any (
        "\\curl.exe", "/curl", "\\wget.exe", "/wget",
        "\\powershell.exe", "\\pwsh.exe", "\\bitsadmin.exe", "\\certutil.exe",
        "\\git.exe", "/git", "\\tar.exe", "/tar", "\\7z.exe",
        "/sh", "/bash", "\\cmd.exe", "\\nc.exe", "/nc", "/ncat"
      )
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Hits = count(), SampleCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)

references:

date: 2026/05/02

High

10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 10 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

CVEsCVE-2026-29199
ATT&CKT1190 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable phpBB Version Inventory (CVE-2026-29199) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] phpBB Authentication Bypass Attempts · [LLM] Anomalous Request to phpBB OAuth Callback (/user/oauth/authenticate/) Without Prior Session · [LLM] phpBB Host Header Injection on Password-Reset Endpoint (CVE-2026-29199)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Remote Code Execution from Web Server Context
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Webshell Persistence in phpBB Upload Directories
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] phpBB DB User Performing Bulk SELECT on phpbb_users or Schema Enumeration · [LLM] Post-Exploitation Network Reconnaissance from Web Server · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Vulnerable phpBB Version Inventory (CVE-2026-29199) AIReconnaissance High
Surface managed Windows/Linux hosts running phpBB at versions <= 3.3.16 or 4.0.0-a2, which are vulnerable to the unauthenticated authentication-bypass + RCE chain. Used to drive patch prioritization to 3.3.17/master. Rationale: Article names exact vulnerable versions (3.3.16 and below, 4.0.0-a2) and fixed version (3.3.17/master). CVE-2026-29199 is the pre-extracted CVE. TVM inventory is the cleanest article-specific pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-29199
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Honeypot/CTF phpBB instance intentionally left unpatched
  • Legacy archived forum read-only behind WAF still flagged as vulnerable
  • Vendor pre-release builds reported as 3.3.17-RC1 mis-parsed as <3.3.17
  • Defender TVM stale inventory after manual patch
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("honeypot", "ctf", "sandbox"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the host is internet-exposed and that phpBB is actually serving traffic (curl /index.php and check the Set-Cookie phpbb3_*_sid). Step 2 (contain): If exposed, gate the box behind WAF block of `/ucp.php?mode=login` from untrusted source IPs and force upgrade to 3.3.17 or master. Step 3 (hunt): For each vulnerable host, run the OAuth callback, host-header, webshell, and RCE-from-web detections below over the last 30 days to verify no prior exploitation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has "phpbb" or SoftwareVendor has "phpbb"
| where SoftwareVersion startswith "3." and SoftwareVersion < "3.3.17"
   or SoftwareVersion == "4.0.0-a2"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where CveId == "CVE-2026-29199") on DeviceId, SoftwareName
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-29199" or (SoftwareName has "phpbb" and (SoftwareVersion < "3.3.17" or SoftwareVersion == "4.0.0-a2"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-29199" OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="phpBB" AND (Vulnerabilities.signature_version<"3.3.17" OR Vulnerabilities.signature_version="4.0.0-a2")) by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.signature_version Vulnerabilities.cve | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-29199" OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="phpBB" AND (Vulnerabilities.signature_version<"3.3.17" OR Vulnerabilities.signature_version="4.0.0-a2")) by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.signature_version Vulnerabilities.cve | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
phpBB Authentication Bypass Attempts AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for HTTP traffic patterns indicative of CVE-2026-29199 abuse: unauthenticated POSTs to phpBB login/UCP endpoints that immediately succeed with a fresh phpbb session cookie, or batched member-list enumeration followed by a single successful UCP request from the same IP. Rationale: Article names the public memberlist ("member list is public, picking a target is trivial") and login endpoints as the attack chain entry point. phpBB-specific paths (`memberlist.php`, `ucp.php?mode=login`, `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword`) are pre-auth and not present in any other software, so the path predicate alone is high-fidelity for phpBB targeting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys/Nuclei) running authenticated baseline scans against your own forum
  • Search-engine crawler walking memberlist + register pages
  • Password-reset flood from legitimate users who forgot creds after a long absence
  • Penetration tester engagement targeting the forum host
Suppression filter
| where not(csUserAgent has_any ("Googlebot", "bingbot", "YandexBot", "Nessus", "Qualys"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pivot on cIP — pull all phpBB requests in the last 24h, look for the memberlist→ucp.php?mode=login pattern + the appearance of a phpbb3_*_sid cookie in the request. Step 2 (contain): If the bypass succeeded (subsequent /adm/index.php hit with auth), revoke all phpBB sessions (`phpbb_sessions` table purge), force password reset, block the source IP at WAF. Step 3 (hunt): Cross-check the OAuth callback UC and the webshell UC for the same DeviceId/Computer in the next 60 minutes.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("HttpConnectionInspected", "ConnectionSuccess")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/memberlist.php", "/ucp.php?mode=login", "/ucp.php?mode=sendpassword", "/ucp.php?mode=register")
| summarize HitCount = count(), Endpoints = make_set(RemoteUrl, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where HitCount >= 5
| where Endpoints has "memberlist.php" and Endpoints has "ucp.php"
| order by HitCount desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any ("/memberlist.php", "/ucp.php")
| extend IsLogin = csUriQuery has "mode=login", IsMemberlist = csUriStem endswith "memberlist.php", IsSendPw = csUriQuery has "mode=sendpassword"
| summarize MemberlistHits = countif(IsMemberlist),
           LoginHits = countif(IsLogin),
           SendPwHits = countif(IsSendPw),
           Successes = countif(scStatus == 200 and IsLogin),
           FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
           LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
           by Computer, cIP, csUserAgent
| where MemberlistHits >= 3 and (LoginHits >= 1 or SendPwHits >= 1)
| order by LastSeen desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR cloudflare OR aws.alb) (@http.url_details.path:*memberlist.php* OR @http.url_details.path:*ucp.php*) (@http.method:POST OR @http.method:GET)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=443)
| ContextImageFileName=/(curl|wget|python|powershell|httpx|nuclei|sqlmap|hydra)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Web.url) as urls dc(Web.url) as url_count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*memberlist.php*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=login*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=sendpassword*" by Web.src Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where url_count >= 3 AND match(urls, "memberlist.php") AND match(urls, "ucp.php")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Web.url) as urls dc(Web.url) as url_count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*memberlist.php*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=login*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=sendpassword*" by Web.src Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where url_count >= 3 AND match(urls, "memberlist.php") AND match(urls, "ucp.php")
Anomalous Request to phpBB OAuth Callback (/user/oauth/authenticate/) Without Prior Session AIDelivery Medium
Hunt for requests to the new 3.3.17 OAuth callback path `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` that originate without a prior outbound redirect to a recognised IdP (Google, Facebook, Bitbucket, LinkedIn). This catches direct/replayed callbacks and reconnaissance for the old vs new OAuth handler that CVE-2026-29199 exploits. Rationale: Article Block 2 names the exact new path `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` (post-patch). Any external scanner probing this URI without a matching IdP-issued state token / referer is either fingerprinting phpBB 3.3.17 or replaying old OAuth callbacks. The path itself is phpBB-exclusive. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356
ATT&CKT1190 T1550.004
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User clicks an OAuth-login button from a bookmarked phpBB tab (no Referer at all)
  • Privacy-conscious browser stripping Referer headers
  • Server-side OAuth library health check from internal monitoring
  • Internal pen-test scanner walking endpoints
Suppression filter
| where not(csReferer has_any ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "healthcheck"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full csUriQuery — legitimate OAuth callbacks carry `state=` and `code=` params. Empty/missing params or non-base64url state is recon. Step 2 (contain): If multiple direct hits from same source IP, WAF-block the IP and inspect server-side phpbb_oauth_states table for orphan entries. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on cIP, look for prior memberlist.php enumeration (other UC) and post-auth /adm/index.php access.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("HttpConnectionInspected", "ConnectionSuccess")
| where RemoteUrl has "/user/oauth/authenticate/"
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("accounts.google.com", "facebook.com", "linkedin.com", "bitbucket.org", "github.com"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem startswith "/user/oauth/authenticate/"
| extend RefererOk = csReferer matches regex @"(?i)(accounts\.google\.com|facebook\.com|linkedin\.com|bitbucket\.org|github\.com)"
| where RefererOk == false
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csHost, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csReferer, csUserAgent, scStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: phpBB OAuth Callback Hit Without IdP Referer

description: Direct request to the new phpBB 3.3.17 OAuth callback `/user/oauth/authenticate/` with no upstream IdP referer — possible replay or recon of CVE-2026-29199 attack surface.

phpBB Host Header Injection on Password-Reset Endpoint (CVE-2026-29199) AIDelivery Low
Hunt web-tier logs for requests to phpBB's password-reset / activation flows where the inbound Host header does not match the server's canonical hostname — a classic primitive for hijacking password-reset emails, which is the most-suspected mechanic behind the CVE-2026-29199 auth-bypass-as-any-user behaviour described in the article. Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-29199 and emphasises that a single unauthenticated request yields a valid session for any user, which strongly points to a password-reset / activation-link hijack chain. The phpBB-specific `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` and `mode=resend_act` paths plus mismatched Host header give a tight pivot. Sentinel query swapped to `Computer` (the actual W3CIISLog column) and `cIP`/`csHost` per the schema. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356
ATT&CKT1190 T1556
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate users coming via legacy alias hostname not in CanonicalHosts list
  • Reverse-proxy / WAF passing through original Host header from internet scans
  • Forum migration period where two hostnames are valid
  • QA / staging hitting prod by accident
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each hit, pull the full request body — confirm `username=` parameter targets a specific account (typically `admin` or a known admin alias). Step 2 (contain): Force password reset on the targeted account, invalidate all sessions in `phpbb_sessions`, and add Host-header validation at the WAF (allow only canonical hosts). Step 3 (hunt): Within 1h of the suspicious request, check for new admin logins to /adm/index.php and the OAuth callback UC.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("HttpConnectionInspected", "ConnectionSuccess")
| where RemoteUrl has "ucp.php" and RemoteUrl has_any ("mode=sendpassword", "mode=resend_act")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com", "community.example.com"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem endswith "ucp.php"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("mode=sendpassword", "mode=resend_act")
| where csMethod == "POST"
| extend HostHeader = tolower(csHost)
| where HostHeader !in~ (CanonicalHosts)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csHost, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csMethod, csUserAgent, scStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR cloudflare OR aws.alb) @http.url_details.path:*ucp.php* (@http.url_details.queryString:*mode=sendpassword* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*mode=resend_act*) @http.method:POST
# log group: /aws/applicationelb/access-logs
fields @timestamp, client_ip, target_status_code, request_url, user_agent, host
| filter request_url like /ucp\.php/
      and (request_url like /mode=sendpassword/ or request_url like /mode=resend_act/)
      and request_verb = "POST"
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=sendpassword*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=resend_act*") AND Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.user_agent _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=sendpassword*" OR Web.url="*ucp.php?mode=resend_act*") AND Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.user_agent _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
Remote Code Execution from Web Server Context AIExploitation High
Catches phpBB RCE after auth-bypass by alerting on child processes spawned from PHP/web-server daemons (apache2, httpd, nginx, php-fpm, w3wp.exe) executing shell interpreters or LOLBin downloaders — the typical post-exploitation pattern when CVE-2026-29199 lands. Rationale: Article confirms RCE as the post-bypass payload. Web-daemon-spawns-shell is the cleanest article-anchored signal because phpBB runs under php/php-fpm/apache/nginx — these parents legitimately almost never spawn /bin/sh or LOLBin downloaders. Reverse-shell tokens (`bash -i`, `/dev/tcp/`) further tighten signal. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB admin running legitimate maintenance hook (e.g., update_check.php exec()ing curl)
  • Custom phpBB MOD/extension that shells out to ImageMagick / ffmpeg
  • Cron-driven backup script invoked from web context
  • Site-builder extension running composer install via shell
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update_check", "composer install", "convert -resize"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the parent process's open file descriptors / lsof to identify which phpBB extension or core file triggered the exec; check the immediately-preceding access.log line for the malicious URL. Step 2 (contain): Kill the child shell, isolate the host from the network, snapshot `/var/www`, rotate any DB/secret pulled into env. Step 3 (hunt): For every other phpBB host in inventory, run the webshell UC and check for /uploads or /store .php drops in the past 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php", "php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wget", "curl", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "python", "python3", "perl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bash -i", "/dev/tcp/", "sh -i", "socket.socket", "base64 -d", "|sh", "|bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php", "php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wget", "curl", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "python", "perl")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bash -i", "/dev/tcp/", "sh -i", "|sh", "|bash", "base64 -d")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Web Server Daemon Spawning Shell or LOLBin (phpBB CVE-2026-29199 Post-Exploit)
id: 7c1b2f4a-d3a1-4c9e-b81d-a90d7e1f1d03
description: Web server / PHP-FPM daemon spawning a shell or download utility — classic phpBB RCE post-exploitation pattern.
references:

    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php'
      - '/php-fpm'

| ImageFileName=/(\/sh|\/bash|\/dash|\/zsh|\\cmd\.exe|\\powershell\.exe|\\pwsh\.exe|\/wget|\/curl|\/nc|\/ncat|\/socat|\/python3?|\/perl)$/i OR CommandLine=/(bash -i|sh -i|\/dev\/tcp\/|\|sh|\|bash|base64 -d)/i

Webshell Persistence in phpBB Upload Directories AIInstallation High
Detects creation of PHP/PHTML/PHP7 files inside phpBB's writable directories (`/store`, `/cache`, `/files`, `/images/avatars/upload`, `/ext`), which are the standard webshell drop locations after a CVE-2026-29199-style admin takeover. Rationale: phpBB ships with `/store`, `/cache`, `/files`, `/images/avatars/upload`, and `/ext` as writable dirs for legitimate runtime use — none of these directories should EVER receive a `.php` file write from a web daemon during normal operation (phpBB writes only data files there). The combination of writable-dir + .php extension + php-fpm/apache parent is a near-zero-FP signal of webshell drop. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?f=14&t=2657356
ATT&CKT1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin installing a new phpBB extension via the extension manager (drops .php files into /ext/ — legitimate)
  • Phpbb upgrade script staging files into /store/
  • Site builder / Composer pulling vendor packages into /ext/
  • Backup utility temporarily restoring .php files from a snapshot
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("phpbb_install", "composer install", "acp_extensions"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Hash the dropped file, run strings + grep for `eval(`, `assert(`, `base64_decode`, `system(`, `passthru(` — webshells almost always have one. Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file, immediately revoke all admin sessions, snapshot the `phpbb_users` and `phpbb_acl_users` tables for backdoor account discovery. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the InitiatingProcessAccountName and look for further file writes in the past 30 days across all phpBB hosts; check apache/nginx logs for the URL that wrote the file.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".php7" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\store\", @"\cache\", @"\files\", @"\images\avatars\upload\", "/store/", "/cache/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php", "php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phtml", "php7", "phar")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/store/", "/cache/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/", "/ext/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP File Dropped in phpBB Writable Directory by Web Daemon
id: 9f3a1b27-c5d6-4f0a-b182-7e2c91a40d04
description: Web daemon (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) writing a PHP/PHTML/PHAR file into phpBB store/cache/files/avatars/ext directory — classic webshell drop after CVE-2026-29199 exploit.
references:

phpBB DB User Performing Bulk SELECT on phpbb_users or Schema Enumeration AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the phpBB database service account issuing high-volume SELECT queries against `phpbb_users` (password hash/credential exfil) or `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` (post-RCE schema discovery), or UNION/INTO OUTFILE patterns indicative of SQLi-via-bypass exploitation. Rationale: Article calls out admin-account takeover unlocking RCE — the typical first post-RCE action is dumping `phpbb_users` (bcrypt hashes, emails) or schema-enumerating for chained SQLi. Strings like `phpbb_users`, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`, `INTO OUTFILE`, `LOAD_FILE(`, `UNION SELECT` are high-signal in the context of a phpBB DB user. CloudWatch query fixed: leading `# log group:` comment + `@timestamp`/`@message` (the reserved CWLI fields) instead of bare `timestamp`/`message`. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/
ATT&CKT1213 T1041 T1190
Data sourcesDatabase
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB admin running a legitimate user-data export via ACP
  • Database backup tool reading from phpbb_users for snapshot
  • MOD/extension running schema migrations that touch INFORMATION_SCHEMA
  • DBA tooling auditing the schema
Suppression filter
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("acp_users", "backup", "mysqldump"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full SQL — distinguish a single `SELECT user_email FROM phpbb_users WHERE user_id=1` (ACP normal) from `SELECT * FROM phpbb_users LIMIT 999999` (exfil). Check what client connected. Step 2 (contain): Rotate the phpBB DB password, kill long-running connections, snapshot the DB for forensics, force a full password reset for all forum users (assume hashes leaked). Step 3 (hunt): Egress-monitor for large outbound transfers from the DB host or the web tier in the prior 24h.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("mysql", "mysql.exe", "mariadb", "psql")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SELECT * FROM phpbb_users", "INFORMATION_SCHEMA", "INTO OUTFILE", "LOAD_FILE(", "UNION SELECT")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php", "php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("daemon", "local0", "local1") and ProcessName has_any ("mysqld", "mariadbd", "postgres")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("phpbb_users", "INFORMATION_SCHEMA", "INTO OUTFILE", "LOAD_FILE(", "UNION SELECT", "phpbb_acl_users", "phpbb_sessions")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(mysql OR mariadb OR postgres OR rds) (@db.user:phpbb* OR @usr.name:phpbb*) (@db.statement:(*phpbb_users* OR *INFORMATION_SCHEMA* OR *"UNION SELECT"* OR *"INTO OUTFILE"* OR *LOAD_FILE*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php|php-fpm|apache2|httpd|nginx|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| ImageFileName=/(mysql|mariadb|psql)(\.exe)?$/i
| CommandLine=/(phpbb_users|INFORMATION_SCHEMA|UNION\s+SELECT|INTO\s+OUTFILE|LOAD_FILE)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/rds/cluster/<phpbb-cluster>/audit
fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /phpbb_users/
      or @message like /INFORMATION_SCHEMA/
      or @message like /UNION\s+SELECT/i
      or @message like /INTO\s+OUTFILE/i
      or @message like /LOAD_FILE\(/i
| filter @message like /\bphpbb\b/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
APPLICATION
index=db_audit OR sourcetype=mysql:audit (user="phpbb" OR user="phpbb_user") (query="*SELECT*FROM*phpbb_users*" OR query="*INFORMATION_SCHEMA*" OR query="*UNION*SELECT*" OR query="*INTO OUTFILE*" OR query="*LOAD_FILE*") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(query) as queries by user src dest | where count > 50 OR match(queries, "UNION|INTO OUTFILE|LOAD_FILE|INFORMATION_SCHEMA")
Post-Exploitation Network Reconnaissance from Web Server AIActions on Objectives High
Detects discovery activity originating from a phpBB web host post-RCE: execution of port-scanners (nmap, masscan), AD enum (net.exe, nltest, adfind), or DNS lookups for internal/private hostnames — indicating attacker pivoting from the forum host into the wider network. Rationale: Web daemons (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) have effectively zero legitimate reason to spawn nmap/masscan/net.exe/nltest/adfind. Article's RCE → admin takeover lifecycle implies the attacker will pivot off the forum host, and the parent-process anchor (php/apache/etc.) keeps this article-specific rather than a generic recon rule. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/
ATT&CKT1046 T1087 T1018
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB admin running a debug dig/nslookup from a web-context script
  • Monitoring agent (Datadog/Nagios) embedded in the same daemon shelling out for diagnostics
  • Container healthcheck using netstat to verify ports
  • Site-reliability ad-hoc curl/dig to validate DNS from web-tier
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "healthcheck", "prometheus"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the recon command's args — broad scan (`nmap -sS 10.0.0.0/16`) vs single-target diag (`dig api.internal`). Capture the parent's open file table to find the dropped script. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the web host from internal subnets via NSG/security group, force kill the recon process tree, snapshot for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): For each scanned IP/CIDR, check downstream SMB/WinRM/SSH auth events from the web host's IP in the next 24h. Cross-reference with the RCE and webshell UCs.
let WebDaemons = dynamic(["php", "php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe"]);
let ReconBins = dynamic(["nmap", "masscan", "arp-scan", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "nltest.exe", "adfind.exe", "netstat", "ss", "ip", "dig", "nslookup"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebDaemons)
| where FileName in~ (ReconBins)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("net view", "net group \"Domain", "nltest /dclist", "nltest /domain_trusts", "Get-ADUser", "Get-ADComputer", "arp -a", "-sn ", "--top-ports")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Pheditor terminal action — directory enumeration via repeated 'dir' probes · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — shell metacharacters in 'dir' POST parameter
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Apache / Nginx / PHP-FPM spawning shell post-Pheditor terminal RCE · [LLM] PHP webshell dropped to webroot by web server user · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48030: Pheditor: OS Command Injection in terminal han
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound C2 from Apache / Nginx / PHP-FPM process to external IP
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — shell metacharacters in 'dir' POST parameter AIExploitation High
Detects POST requests to pheditor.php with action=terminal where the body contains shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, double-ampersand, backtick, $()) — the precise exploit signature for CVE-2026-48030 OS command injection via the unsanitized 'dir' parameter. Rationale: Article quotes the exact PoC: 'dir=/tmp; curl -s https://ifconfig.me #' bypassing the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist that only guards $command. The detection targets the four metacharacters the article calls out explicitly (`&`, `;`, `||`) plus `$(` and backtick which are equivalent injection vectors, in both raw and URL-encoded form (curl --data-urlencode produces the encoded variant). Cross-checked against the GitHub Advisory page. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin pasting a multi-command sequence into the terminal field — e.g. 'cd /var/log && tail -f syslog' — the && reaches the dir parameter
  • Penetration test against pheditor itself, where the test team is intentionally exploiting CVE-2026-48030
  • WAF testing / DAST scanner (Burp Active Scan, Acunetix) probing the terminal endpoint with metacharacter payloads
  • Legitimate use of paths containing semicolons on rare filesystems (extremely uncommon on Linux but possible on SMB-mounted shares)
Suppression filter
| where not (cIP in ("10.0.0.5","10.0.0.6") and UA has "PenTestTeam")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full POST body from WAF/proxy. Confirm action=terminal AND a shell metacharacter inside the dir= value. Identify the authenticated session (session cookie, source IP). Check pheditor version on the host — vulnerable if 2.0.1–2.0.3. Step 2 — Contain: block the source IP at the WAF/edge. Disable the compromised pheditor session (clear server-side session). Take the pheditor instance offline or restrict to localhost until patched. Rotate the pheditor admin password. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC2 (web-server shell spawn), UC3 (webshell file write), UC4 (outbound C2 from web user) on the same host within the next 60 minutes. Inventory the webroot for new .php files modified after the POST timestamp. Check whether the pheditor admin password was previously brute-forced or leaked.
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WebLogs = union isfuzzy=true 
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours) | where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem endswith "pheditor.php" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, Path=csUriStem, Body=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus)),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours) | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has "pheditor.php" | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, cIP=SourceIP, csMethod=RequestMethod, Path=RequestURL, Body=Message, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome));
WebLogs
| where Body has "action=terminal" or Body has "action%3Dterminal"
| where Body matches regex @"(?i)dir=[^&]*(;|\||&&|%3B|%7C|%26%26|%24%28|%60|`)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, Path, Body, UA, Status
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 Shell Metacharacters in dir POST Parameter
id: a3f7b2c8-1e4d-4f9a-8b6c-7d2e9f1a4b3c
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php with shell metacharacters in the dir POST parameter, indicating exploitation of CVE-2026-48030 OS command injection.

author: Detection Engineering

  - attack.initial_access

  action:

WEB

| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Web.uri_path) as uri_path, values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua, values(Web.src) as src, values(Web.dest) as dest, values(Web.http_content) as body from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="*pheditor.php*" Web.http_method="POST" (Web.http_content="*action=terminal*" OR Web.http_content="*action%3Dterminal*") (Web.http_content="*dir=*;*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*|*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*&&*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%3B*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%7C*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%24%28*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%60*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.user, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.uri_path) as uri_path, values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua, values(Web.src) as src, values(Web.dest) as dest, values(Web.http_content) as body from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="*pheditor.php*" Web.http_method="POST" (Web.http_content="*action=terminal*" OR Web.http_content="*action%3Dterminal*") (Web.http_content="*dir=*;*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*|*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*&&*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%3B*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%7C*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%24%28*" OR Web.http_content="*dir=*%60*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.user, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")`
Apache / Nginx / PHP-FPM spawning shell post-Pheditor terminal RCE AIInstallation High
Hunts for shell or network-tool binaries spawned by web server processes (httpd, apache2, nginx, php-fpm) running under www-data/apache/nginx accounts — the canonical post-exploitation pattern when CVE-2026-48030 (or any PHP RCE) is successfully exercised. Rationale: Article PoC ends with `uid=33(www-data)` — confirming the exploit runs as the web server user. After the dir injection, the unsanitized parameter is concatenated into a shell_exec() call, so child processes of apache2/nginx/php-fpm under www-data running shells or network tools is the highest-fidelity post-exploit signal. Cross-referenced with the Sigma community rule 'Webshell Hacking Activity Patterns' and Falcon CrowdStrike's standard web-RCE detection logic. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PHP exec()/system() in a deployed application (cron-style PHP shelling out to gzip a log)
  • System administrators running shell commands directly on the host (rare for www-data — should be excluded by user filter)
  • Composer / dependency installation scripts that legitimately spawn curl/wget as www-data during deployment
  • Monitoring agents (Datadog, New Relic) shelling out from PHP-FPM workers to gather host metrics
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","php artisan","wp-cli"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full process tree (ancestor chain) and command line for the child process. Look for telltale strings: reverse-shell connectors (`bash -i`, `/dev/tcp/`, `nc -e`), download commands (`curl http://`, `wget http://`), or staging directories (`/tmp/`, `/dev/shm/`). Step 2 — Contain: kill the offending process tree. Isolate the host from the network if a reverse shell is confirmed. Quarantine any files written under /tmp or /dev/shm by www-data in the last hour. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC1 (was there a Pheditor POST that triggered this?), UC3 (webshell on disk?), UC4 (any outbound from www-data?). Pull the apache/nginx access log for the 60 seconds preceding the process spawn — the triggering POST will be there. Check authentication logs for the pheditor session that was leveraged.
let LookbackHours = 24h;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpd","apache2","nginx","php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php")
| where FileName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where AccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","httpd","nobody","http","_www")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackHours = 24h;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("httpd","apache2","nginx","php-fpm","php")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","httpd","nobody","http","_www")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
