PHP webshell dropped to webroot by web server user AIInstallation High
Detects creation of .php / .phtml / .phar files in common webroot paths by web server processes running as www-data/apache/nginx — the article shows the attacker writing a webshell to /var/www/html/shell.php via the dir-parameter injection. Rationale: PoC Step 5 in the article literally writes `<?php system($_GET['c']);?>` to /var/www/html/shell.php as www-data. The detection mirrors that exact pattern: PHP file extension + webroot path + web-server account. Cross-checked against MITRE T1505.003 Web Shell technique page and Sigma rule sigma/rules/linux/file_event/file_event_lnx_php_webshell.yml. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate application deployments writing PHP files (composer install, git pull from deployment automation) — usually runs as deploy user not www-data, but PHP-FPM-driven WordPress auto-updates do hit this
  • WordPress / Drupal / Joomla auto-update writing plugin or theme PHP files as www-data — common false positive on shared hosting
  • Cache file generation by some PHP frameworks (Symfony, Laravel) writing .php files to var/cache — typically not in webroot but worth checking
  • Custom CMS user-uploaded template files written by an authenticated PHP process
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cron","wp-admin/update","drush","composer install","composer update","git pull"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: download (don't execute) the newly written PHP file. Inspect for webshell indicators: `system($_GET`, `eval($_POST`, `assert(`, `passthru(`, `shell_exec(`, base64-encoded payloads. Compare against legitimate CMS update file lists (WordPress / Drupal core file manifest). Step 2 — Contain: quarantine the file (move to /tmp/quarantine or compute SHA256 and delete). Block web access to the path. Reload web server config. If WordPress/Drupal, force core integrity check. Step 3 — Hunt: any other .php files written by www-data in the last 7 days? Outbound connections from www-data after the file write? GET requests to the new file in access logs? Pivot to UC1 (Pheditor POST that triggered the write) and UC4 (subsequent C2).
let LookbackHours = 24h;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www","/srv/www","/usr/share/nginx/html","/opt/lampp/htdocs","/var/lib/apache2")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".php5"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","httpd","nobody","http","_www")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackHours = 24h;

| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www","/srv/www","/usr/share/nginx/html","/opt/lampp/htdocs","/var/lib/apache2")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","php5","phar")

title: PHP Webshell Written to Webroot by Web Server User

description: Detects creation of PHP files in common webroot directories by web server processes running as www-data, apache, or nginx — classic webshell drop following RCE (as in CVE-2026-48030 PoC).

Outbound C2 from Apache / Nginx / PHP-FPM process to external IP AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections from web server processes (or shells/curl/wget spawned by them) running as www-data/apache/nginx, to non-RFC1918 IP space — the article's PoC includes `curl -s https://ifconfig.me` as the proof of RCE, the same shape used for C2 callback. Rationale: PoC Step 4 in the article uses `curl -s https://ifconfig.me` from www-data — proving outbound from web server context. Whether confirming RCE (ifconfig.me) or staging C2 (reverse shell), the network shape is the same: web-server user making outbound to non-RFC1918. Cross-referenced with MITRE T1071.001 and Sigma's network_connection_lnx_susp_outbound rules. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP app legitimately calling external APIs (Stripe, Twilio, S3, third-party SaaS) from PHP-FPM — high noise on commerce sites
  • WordPress / Drupal core/plugin update checks fetching update manifests from wordpress.org / drupal.org
  • Composer / npm / pip running as www-data during in-place deployments fetching dependencies from packagist.org / npmjs.org / pypi.org
  • Outbound NTP, DNS, or monitoring agent traffic mistakenly attributed to web server PIDs
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("api.wordpress.org","updates.drupal.org","packagist.org","api.stripe.com","api.github.com","github.com"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: check the destination IP/domain against threat intel (VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, abuse.ch). Look at the source process command line — `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/...` or `curl -d @/etc/passwd` is unambiguous. Resolve the destination — fresh / low-reputation / dynamic-DNS is a strong signal. Step 2 — Contain: block the destination at the egress firewall. Kill the web server worker process making the connection. If reverse shell confirmed, isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC1 (preceding Pheditor POST), UC2 (parent web-server spawning curl/wget/nc), UC3 (any webshell on disk). Pull 24h of outbound from this host's www-data user — look for beacon patterns (regular interval, same destination). Check other Pheditor instances in the fleet for the same destination IP.
let LookbackHours = 24h;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpd","apache2","nginx","php-fpm","php","sh","bash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","httpd","nobody","http","_www")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackHours = 24h;

| where SrcUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","httpd","nobody","http","_www")
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr)) and DstIpAddr !startswith "127."
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor terminal action — directory enumeration via repeated 'dir' probes AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for repeated POSTs to pheditor.php with action=terminal from the same source enumerating multiple distinct 'dir' values within a short window — pre-exploitation reconnaissance pattern where an attacker maps the host filesystem before launching the dir-injection payload. Rationale: Article's PoC walks the attacker through discovery (Step 3 — probe what's blocked) before exploit (Step 4 — the bypass). A realistic attacker probes the filesystem layout via the dir parameter before injecting (testing /tmp, /var/www, /etc, etc.). Volumetric/distinct count on the dir parameter from one source within a 10-min window catches reconnaissance regardless of whether the payload triggers UC1 — gives early warning of exploitation in progress. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1083 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin using pheditor's terminal feature to browse the filesystem (their valid use case — distinguishable by csUserName but the source IP is typically corporate)
  • Vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Nuclei) probing the endpoint with multiple dir values during authenticated scans
  • Penetration test against pheditor verifying CVE-2026-48030
  • Misbehaving frontend JavaScript on the pheditor UI that pre-fetches multiple directories on page load
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("10.0.0.5","10.0.0.6")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull all POST bodies from this source IP in the window. Look at the dir values — `/`, `/etc`, `/root`, `/var/www`, `/home` is enumeration; `/tmp` + `/tmp` + `/tmp` is normal use. Check the authenticated username against expected pheditor admins. Step 2 — Contain: if the source IP is external and not an authorised admin, block at the WAF and invalidate the session. Force a password reset on the pheditor admin account that was used. Patch pheditor to >= 2.0.4 (post-fix replacing the unsanitized $dir with escapeshellarg). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC1 (did any of these probes contain shell metacharacters?), UC2/UC3/UC4 (did exploitation succeed on this host?). Check whether the same source IP enumerated other web apps. Review pheditor authentication logs for brute-force preceding this activity.
let LookbackHours = 6h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinDistinctDirs = 5;
let WebLogs = union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours) | where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem endswith "pheditor.php" | project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUserName, Body=csUriQuery),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours) | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has "pheditor.php" | project TimeGenerated, cIP=SourceIP, csUserName=SourceUserName, Body=Message);
WebLogs
| where Body has "action=terminal" or Body has "action%3Dterminal"
| extend DirParam = extract(@"(?i)(?:^|&)dir=([^&\s]+)", 1, Body)
| where isnotempty(DirParam)
| summarize DistinctDirs = dcount(DirParam), TotalRequests = count(), DirsSample = make_set(DirParam, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by cIP, csUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctDirs >= MinDistinctDirs
| order by DistinctDirs desc
